__comment: Library modules under src/lib that nothing imports. The gate in src/lib/orphan-detect.test.ts asserts current_orphans is a SUBSET of this list, so a NEW orphan fails CI while an existing one does not. The list may only shrink. When you wire, merge or remove a module, delete its entry in the same commit â€” the gate does not fail on an entry that has stopped being an orphan, so cleanup is never blocked. Target: {}.
howToClear: For each entry: (1) verify the implementation and its tests, (2) identify the intended consumer, (3) decide wire / merge / migrate / deprecate / remove, (4) if wiring, add an integration test, (5) delete the entry here.
measurement: Detector: src/lib/orphan-detect.ts. Scans 612 modules under src/lib against every source file in src/, scripts/ and mail-engine/. Matching is textual and deliberately generous â€” a dynamic import(variable) is invisible to it â€” so a flagged module still needs a human decision, but an unflagged one is genuinely referenced somewhere. Measured 27 on 2026-08-16; 26 after attendance-lapse.ts was wired.

aes-engine.why: The AES engine's provider and simulation modules. /aquintutor/aes-console runs six engines live, but these six files are not among the ones it imports. Either the console should offer them or they are a previous iteration; nobody has decided which.
aes-engine.decision: UNDECIDED - needs a product call before any code moves

ask-surfaces.why: Three answering surfaces (employee, visitor, and their shared log) with no route behind them. ask-aquin.ts IS wired; these three are a parallel implementation for different audiences that never got a door.
ask-surfaces.decision: WIRE OR MERGE - overlaps ask-aquin.ts, so compare the two before wiring either

assistant.why: Tested and unreachable. answer.ts and scope.ts each have their own suite and no consumer, which is the most convincing kind of dead code because it looks maintained.
assistant.decision: WIRE - an assistant with a passing test suite and no entry point is a built feature with no door

hr-unwired.why: org-backfill.ts repairs the org graph and nothing calls it. attendance-lapse.ts was in this group and has been WIRED: src/lib/hr/scheduled.ts runs the assessment, /api/cron/hr-sweep is its door, and the schedule is registered in vercel.json and CONFIGURED_CRONS.
hr-unwired.decision: WIRE TO THE SCHEDULER - handler first, then the route, then the schedule. A cron entry pointing at nothing is a guaranteed nightly failure.

board.why: board-translate.ts and recognition-event.ts are exercised only by board-live.test.ts. The live teaching board imports neither.
board.decision: UNDECIDED - may be groundwork for the A2 speech seam that has not landed yet

learning-unwired.why: course-access.ts and course-builder.ts have no importer. The LMS spine builds on training_courses directly, so these are probably an earlier parallel implementation.
learning-unwired.decision: MERGE OR REMOVE - compare against the LMS spine before deleting anything

mail-infrastructure.why: Infrastructure primitives written ahead of their consumers. cors.ts and service-auth.ts are tested and called by nothing; mailplatform/automation.ts is exercised only by mailplatform-core.test.ts. This is a parallel mail-platform effort in progress.
mail-infrastructure.decision: WIRE - service-auth.ts in particular guards the app-to-mail-host boundary, and a boundary primitive nothing routes through provides no protection

platform-misc.why: capability-coverage.ts, match.ts, person-360.ts, providers/video.ts and founder-console-view.ts each have no importer. person-360 and capability-coverage look like reporting surfaces that were never given a page; founder-console-view has its own test suite.
platform-misc.decision: UNDECIDED - assess individually; several are probably one page away from being useful

tooling.why: Used only by tests, and correctly so. test-shim.ts is the house synchronous test runner imported by eighteen suites; orphan-detect.ts is the detector powering this very gate. Neither is a product capability and neither should ever have a production consumer.
tooling.decision: KEEP - the only two entries expected to remain permanently

talent-stack-fork.why: TWO parallel talent stacks now exist in this tree and neither is wired. src/lib/talent/* is the tal_* stack (docs/talent-to-org/TALENT_TO_ORG_MASTER_SPEC.md); src/lib/talentos/* is a tos_* stack built against docs/talent-os-spec.md. They model the same domain - person, codes, onboarding - with different table prefixes and different vocabularies. sources.ts is the tal_* recruitment PROVENANCE registry (spec 15/F5) and is deliberately separate from src/lib/application-sources.ts, which keeps candidate-declared ATTRIBUTION; it is waiting on an ingestion route to call it. talentos/person.ts is the tos_* person resolver. Neither is dead by accident - both are complete, commented and, in person.ts's case, tested.
talent-stack-fork.decision: BLOCKED ON A PRODUCT CALL - the fork must be resolved before either is wired. Pick one stack; the loser is removed, not left beside the winner. Wiring either now doubles the surface that has to be migrated later. sources.ts is WIRE-ON-INGESTION once tal_* is the chosen stack.
